summary.headline: Sasken Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹339 Cr, with software services margin up 240 bps to 30.6% while Product Solutions margin fell to 5.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 24% YoY and 1.6% QoQ to ₹339 Cr, led by Software Services at ₹219 Cr (+24.3% YoY). Product Solutions revenue was ₹120 Cr (+23.6% YoY, -3.9% QoQ) after a strong Q4, with memory availability and component pricing pressure. Gross margin was 21.9% (₹74 Cr), and EBIT margin was 6.3%, while PAT was ₹23 Cr (6.9% margin) and was hit by normalisation of Q4 other-income one-offs. Order booking was US$47 million TCV, including US$34 million of new deal wins, with five new logos added.

financial_highlights.change: -310 bps QoQ (Keshav Sureka cited 12.8% prior period)
Sequential decline from Q4 one-off other income and lower FX gains

segments.name: Software Services
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹219 Cr, up 24.3% YoY and 4.8% QoQ; gross margin expanded 240 bps to 30.6% on utilisation, cost discipline and scale. Management says the segment grew more than 20% YoY.

segments.name: Product Solutions (incl. Borqs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹120 Cr, up 23.6% YoY but down 3.9% QoQ; gross margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0% in Q4 (per the 310 bps decline) due to memory cost pass-through, lower incremental margin and silicon productization mix. Management expects margins to stabilise over the full year.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management said it will maintain margins while growing, using efficiency and value pricing.
Management targets US$4 million run-rate revenue for 93 active customers under its 60x4x3 strategy; timeline may stretch by one or two years beyond three.
Breakeven for Borqs at about US$12 million quarterly revenue, per CFO.
Expect large cash consumption in FY27 from working capital and fixed assets; management is working toward cash-flow positive, using internal accruals and external funds.
capex_capacity: Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi to build semiconductor talent.
Opened a new centre of excellence in Hyderabad.
Inventory build in Q1 to manage memory shortage contributed to negative cash flow; some silicon products ship through the year.
Silicon business is shifting toward productization; capacity expansion requires working capital.
demand_pricing: Order booking US$47 million TCV (US$34 million new), ACV about US$40 million (US$24 million new); the TCV is not total backlog, and management targets a 9–10 month revenue carry.
Five new logos; 93 active customers vs 79 a year ago; top-five customer share ~56% (vs ~52% previously).
Two hyperscaler engagements (different hyperscalers): a multi-year capability engagement and an OS sustenance engagement, plus an AI and automation deal covering agentic AI and LLM validation.
CSAT 4.5 out of 5 vs industry benchmark 3.75.
Revenue mix: North America 30%, EMEA ~25%, India 26%, APAC ~20%.
Automotive: Borqs instrument cluster module ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive; no commercial order yet.
Memory pricing and component costs are being passed through to customers, but incremental margin is not recovered.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer wins and Software Services margins, but cautious and non-committal on Product Solutions margins and cash flow. Management declined to give margin guidance, disclosed no project-level detail, and deferred on specific partnership and order-level questions.
key_quotes: We will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum.
So, we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time, but as Rajiv mentioned, right, so we are constantly making sure that we are driving efficiencies in how we are doing.
So, it is a function of how the customer does the offtake of some of these products.

qa_highlights.question: What pipeline of accounts could cross the US$4 million run-rate threshold in FY27, given customer count rose from 79 to 93 and top-five concentration rose to about 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the 60x4x3 target (US$4 million run-rate for 93 active customers within three years) is still the goal; the three-year timeline is metaphoric and may stretch one or two more years. Specific FY27 target accounts were not named, and sales bandwidth is being added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Product Solutions gross margin drop from 12.8% to 5.9%: memory pricing or something else?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said memory cost pass-through removes incremental margin even though costs are passed on, and the silicon business shifting toward productization changed mix. Some products ship through the year, so margins should be read on a full-year basis and are expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two hyperscaler engagements with the same hyperscaler or different ones?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody confirmed they are different hyperscalers.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount rose about 9% QoQ while cost rose only about 3%; how will sales and senior analog/RF leadership headcount evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said at least five to six more sales heads will be added in the rest of the year, with some growth delivery-led. Priyaranjan said cost mix includes lateral and fresher hires and Q4 had non-recurring bonus catch-up; utilisation improved. Anup Savla said the teams are independent and senior niche analog/RF/mmWave skills are grown in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 60x4x3 target of US$4 million run-rate be reached if extended by a couple of years, and at what growth drivers, with growth at the expense of margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said the company may take one more year, not a commitment to a number, and cited silicon, specialised silicon, devices (China-plus-one and Make in India) and full-stack software services as the three vectors. On margins, he said Software Services margins went from about 2-3% to 11.5-12% EBIT over six quarters and the company will maintain margins while growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue stay flat for years and then grow suddenly in software services?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan cited four changes: working closer to customers, empowering teams to own growth, investing in capability, and filling white spaces such as the Borqs and silicon acquisitions for end-to-end engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow been negative for two years despite profit growth, and will FY27 be cash-flow positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said cash outflow reflects investment in working capital and fixed assets, not collection problems; a large cash consumption is expected this year, Q1 included inventory build for memory shortage. Funding will come from internal accruals and external funds, and the cash-flow positive timeline is work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Borqs break-even point still hold at the earlier US$60-70 million top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said break-even is now about US$12 million of quarterly revenue, after which the business adds to the bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of GlobalFoundries and Intel IP certifications and the formal TSMC relationship?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said all three are in progress with substantial progress, leading to more design activity, but no announcements can be made yet due to the non-public nature of the work.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RF and mmWave projects and when will revenue from these niche technologies show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said projects span connectivity, automotive interfaces and power, and revenue mix already reflects such implementation, though project details were not disclosed. Hareesh Ramanna said the Borqs instrument-cluster module is ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive, so no commercial order is yet in hand.

risks_watch: Product Solutions gross margin at 5.9% (down 310 bps QoQ) with memory cost pass-through leaving no incremental margin; watch whether margins stabilise over FY27 as management expects.
Negative operating cash flow for two years; management expects large cash consumption in FY27 and has not given a timeline to cash-flow positive. Watch working capital and any external funding.
The US$4 million run-rate per-customer target has slipped in timing by one to two years beyond the three-year goal; the 60x4x3 timeline and the 93-customer base remain unproven.
Top-five customer concentration rose to about 56% from about 52%, and the sales team is being expanded by only five to six heads.
Borqs automotive instrument-cluster module has no commercial order yet, facing price competition from Chinese-sourced modules; the TCV-to-revenue conversion (9-10 month carry) also needs tracking.

adds.what: Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi (talent, not productive capacity)
New centre of excellence in Hyderabad

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management declined to guide margins and said it will maintain margins while growing. Growth backed partially by US$34M new TCV (US$24M new ACV), five new logos and 93 active customers, but no specific capacity additions, and Borqs has no commercial automotive order yet.
